ao_demand_evidence.input:
Construct a dichotomous key to identify specimens A to D, using only the observations in this table.
| Specimen | Jointed legs | Leg pairs | Antennae pairs |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| A | absent | 0 | 0 |
| B | present | 3 | 1 |
| C | present | 4 | 0 |
| D | present | 5 | 2 |
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: One possible key: 1a Jointed legs absent → A; 1b Jointed legs present → 2. 2a Two pairs of antennae → D; 2b Fewer than two pairs of antennae → 3. 3a Three pairs of legs → B; 3b Four pairs of legs → C. Any key that separates all four specimens correctly is credited.

ao_demand_evidence.input:
Use this key to name the letter reached by each of four animals. (i) no jointed legs; (ii) jointed legs, no antennae; (iii) jointed legs, one pair of antennae; (iv) jointed legs, two pairs of antennae.
1a Jointed legs absent → A
1b Jointed legs present → go to 2
2a Antennae absent → C
2b Antennae present → go to 3
3a One pair of antennae → B
3b Two pairs of antennae → D

Observe a common local invertebrate animal, such as a beetle, an ant, a woodlouse or a snail. Draw a labelled line drawing of it, showing its relative proportions, and label at least two features that show which group it belongs to.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A line drawing with a clear, continuous outline and no shading; the main parts in realistic relative sizes; ruled label lines that end on the structures; at least two labels naming features that show the group. For an ant: three body regions, three pairs of legs on the thorax and one pair of antennae, labelled head, thorax, abdomen, leg and antenna.
